To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the CAPN316 SNP in CAPN1, the UASMS2 SNP in LEP and the GHR-1 SNP in GHR were significantly associated with meat quality in commercial Aberdeen Angus-sired crossbred cattle.

the CAPN1 SNP CAPN316 was associated with tenderness and hindquarter weight; the LEP SNP UASMS2 was associated with overall liking; the GHR SNP GHR1 was associated with odour; and the DGAT1 SNP DGAT1 was associated with sir loin weight and fat depth.
we found that the CAPN1 SNP was associated with tenderness, the LEP SNP with overall liking, the GHR SNP with odour and the DGAT1 SNP with sirloin and fat depth surrounding this cut.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of genetic markers for meat quality in cattle and their incorporation into a commercial beef breeding program.
the identification of genes that affect meat quality traits in cattle.
the genetic control of meat quality in cattle, and the aim is to improve the efficiency of beef production.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the CAPN1 SNP is a useful tool for predicting tenderness in beef and that the LEP SNP could be useful in predicting overall liking in beef.
the results of this study indicate that the SNP CAPN316, UASMS, GHR-2 and DGAT1 are associated with meat quality traits, and therefore may be used in selection schemes.
the results of this study are of value to the industry and the scientific community.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the CAPN1 SNP, CAPN316 is the most useful for improving meat quality.
the CAPN1 SNP, CAPN316 and DGAT1 SNP, UASMS3 are the most important SNPs for meat quality in commercial cattle.
we have identified some associations between SNP in the CAP1, LEP, GHR, and DGAT1 genes and meat quality, which are worth further investigation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the CAPN1, LEP and DGAT1 genes have the greatest potential to be incorporated into a breeding programme to improve meat quality in the future.
the CAPN1 SNP is associated with tenderness in both the taste panel and mechanical tenderness, which has been shown to be a reliable indicator of eating quality in the UK.
